title: Cycle Budget Calculator
description: An Apply-level calculator where students set clock speed and a real-time deadline to compute the available CPU-cycle budget, then compare it against a sample workload on a capacity bar.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Embedded Systems
Real-Time Computing

learningObjectives: Calculate a cycle budget from clock speed and deadline
Judge whether a given workload fits within a budget
Explain the trade-off between clock speed and deadline
prerequisites: A CPU executes a fixed number of cycles per second

controls.label: Show formula
controls.purpose: Reveal the general equation with units

assumptions: The CPU is fully available to this task for the whole deadline window
One instruction-cycle accounting unit; no stalls or interrupts modeled
limitations: Real systems lose cycles to interrupts, memory stalls, and DMA contention, so usable headroom is always smaller than the ideal figure shown

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict-then-check parameter exploration with a deliberately failing default
keyQuestions: Why is the capacity bar fully red on load?
What is the minimum clock speed that fits the default workload?
commonMisconceptions: That a faster clock always solves a missed deadline regardless of power budget
Forgetting to convert milliseconds to seconds before multiplying
assessmentOpportunities: Compute the budget for 133 MHz with a 25 ms deadline and judge whether a 4,000,000-cycle workload fits
